headline: Theft of two Renoir paintings reignites debate over vulnerability of French museums
description: Stolen from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer on Tuesday, the paintings add to a growing list of artworks taken in recent months, a trend that prompted the French minister of culture to announce an emergency action plan in July.

headline: China's forbidden memory of the greatest famine in history
description: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (2/7). The Great Leap Forward, imposed on China by Mao Zedong from 1958 to 1961, triggered one of the deadliest famines in human history. In rural areas, especially in Henan province, where peasants paid the heaviest price for this economic policy, the topic remains taboo.

Fifty years after Mao's death, China still grapples with his legacy
description: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (1/7). Mao Zedong, who died on September 9, 1976, founded the People's Republic of China and still casts a shadow over the country's political life. The Chinese Communist Party, whose power base Mao established, remains divided between loyalty to his myth and condemnation of his 'mistakes,' which led to the deaths of tens of millions of people.

headline: Ahead of Pope Leo's visit to France, Church and authorities expect record crowds
description: Leo XIV is scheduled to visit France from September 25 to 28. Hundreds of thousands of faithful are expected in the streets of the capital, where the pontiff will spend two days, and 80,000 young people are set to take part in a vigil at the Stade de France.
byline: Antoine Albertini,  Hélène Bekmezian and  Sarah Belouezzane

headline: Mario Draghi, the 'sphinx' still shaping the EU's agenda
description: At 79, the former president of the European Central Bank, who no longer holds any official office, remains at the heart of European Union politics. Elusive and deliberately secretive, he skillfully leverages his ability to speak to political leaders, business executives, and financial markets alike.
byline: Allan Kaval,  Eric Albert and  Sophie Fay
